scenes.title: Athena Kindles Diomedes
scenes.summary: Athena gives Diomedes might and daring so that he may win noble fame, and fire blazes from his helmet and shield like the star of late summer.

scenes.title: The Sons of Dares
scenes.summary: Diomedes kills Phegeus, son of Dares, priest of Hephaestus; Hephaestus hides the other son, Idaeus, in darkness so that the old man is not left wholly bereaved.

scenes.title: Athena Leads Ares Away
scenes.summary: Athena takes Ares by the hand and persuades him to leave the mortals to fight it out; she seats him on the banks of the Scamander.

scenes.title: Each Leader Takes His Man
scenes.summary: The Trojans give way, and each Achaean leader kills a man: Agamemnon kills Odius, Idomeneus Phaestus, Menelaus the hunter Scamandrius, Meriones Phereclus the shipbuilder, Meges Pedaeus, and Eurypylus Hypsenor, priest's son.

scenes.title: Pandarus Wounds Diomedes
scenes.summary: Diomedes sweeps across the plain like a river in flood until Pandarus shoots him in the shoulder and boasts. Sthenelus draws out the arrow; Diomedes prays to Athena, who strengthens him, takes the mist from his eyes so that he can tell gods from men, and forbids him to fight any god but Aphrodite.

scenes.title: Diomedes Rages
scenes.summary: Wounded like a lion in a sheepfold, Diomedes returns three times as fierce and kills Astynous and Hypeiron; Abas and Polyidus, sons of the dream-reader Eurydamas; Xanthus and Thoon, the only sons of old Phaenops; and two sons of Priam.

scenes.title: Aeneas and Pandarus
scenes.summary: Aeneas finds Pandarus, who regrets that he left his horses at home and brought only a useless bow. They mount Aeneas' chariot together. Sthenelus urges retreat; Diomedes refuses, and tells him to seize Aeneas' horses, of the breed Zeus gave to Tros for Ganymede.

scenes.title: The Death of Pandarus
scenes.summary: Pandarus' spear pierces Diomedes' shield but not his corselet; Diomedes' spear, guided by Athena, strikes Pandarus in the face and kills him. Aeneas bestrides the body like a lion, and Diomedes crushes his hip with a stone that two men of today could not lift.

scenes.title: Aphrodite Wounded
scenes.summary: Aphrodite wraps Aeneas in her robe and carries him off; Sthenelus drives away Aeneas' horses. Diomedes pursues the goddess and wounds her hand, and ichor flows. She drops her son, whom Apollo hides in a cloud, and Diomedes taunts her.

scenes.title: Aphrodite on Olympus
scenes.summary: Iris leads Aphrodite to Ares, who lends her his chariot to Olympus. Dione comforts her daughter with stories of gods who suffered at mortal hands, Ares, Hera and Hades, and warns of Diomedes' fate. Athena and Hera mock her, and Zeus tells her that the works of war are not hers.

scenes.title: Apollo Stops Diomedes
scenes.summary: Diomedes attacks Aeneas three times under Apollo's protection; at the fourth, Apollo warns him that gods and men are not alike. Apollo takes Aeneas to Pergamus to be healed, leaves a phantom for the armies to fight over, and sends Ares to rouse the Trojans in the likeness of Acamas.

scenes.title: Sarpedon Rebukes Hector
scenes.summary: Sarpedon reproaches Hector for leaving the fighting to the allies. Hector rallies the Trojans; the Achaeans, whitened by dust like winnowers by chaff, hold firm. Ares covers the battle in night, and Apollo sends Aeneas back healed.

scenes.title: The Battle Renewed
scenes.summary: The Achaeans stand like motionless clouds. Agamemnon exhorts them and kills Deicoon; Aeneas kills the twins Crethon and Orsilochus, who fall like fir trees. Menelaus and Antilochus drive Aeneas off and kill Pylaemenes and his charioteer Mydon.

scenes.title: Hector and Ares
scenes.summary: Hector charges with Ares and Enyo beside him. Diomedes, recognizing the god, recoils like a traveler at a flooding river and tells the Achaeans to give ground. Hector kills two men; Ajax kills Amphius but is driven back.

scenes.title: Tlepolemus and Sarpedon
scenes.summary: Tlepolemus, son of Heracles, taunts Sarpedon, son of Zeus, with Heracles' sack of Troy; Sarpedon kills him and is wounded in the thigh. Odysseus kills seven Lycians until Hector comes. Under Zeus's oak, Pelagon draws the spear from Sarpedon, who faints and revives in the North Wind.

scenes.title: Hector and Ares Advance
scenes.summary: The Achaeans give ground without turning, and Hector and Ares kill six more men.

scenes.title: Hera and Athena Arm
scenes.summary: Hera harnesses her horses to a chariot of gold, silver and bronze while Athena puts on the tunic of Zeus, the aegis with Rout, Strife and the Gorgon's head, and her golden helmet. The Hours open the gates of heaven; Zeus lets them punish Ares, and they drive to the rivers of Troy.

scenes.title: Athena and Diomedes
scenes.summary: Hera, in the likeness of Stentor, shames the Argives. Athena finds Diomedes resting his wound and reproaches him with his father Tydeus; he answers that he is obeying her command not to fight the gods, and she releases him to strike Ares.

scenes.title: Diomedes Wounds Ares
scenes.summary: Athena takes Sthenelus' place in the chariot, wearing the helmet of Hades. Ares, stripping Periphas, attacks; Athena turns his spear aside and drives Diomedes' spear into his belly. Ares bellows like ten thousand men and rises into the sky like a dark cloud.

scenes.title: Ares Healed
scenes.summary: Ares shows Zeus his wound and complains of Athena; Zeus calls him the most hateful of the gods but has Paeëon heal him, as fig juice curdles milk. Hebe bathes him, and Hera and Athena return to the house of Zeus.

days.label: Day 22
days.note: The battle that began at 4.446 continues through the whole of Book 5 and on into Book 6.
